newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PROTESTERS CLASH WITH POLICE AT PRESIDENCY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PROTESTERS CLASH WITH POLICE AT PRESIDENCY.

text.p: Bulgarian opposition protesters clashed with police outside the presidency on Saturday as President Zhelyu Zhelev met political leaders to discuss the country's deepening political crisis.
A reporter inside the presidency said police were using clubs to disperse 500 protesters with clubs, and police reinforcements were arriving.
After a day and a night of clashes outside parliament in which 97 people were hurt, Zhelev said he would not ask the ruling Socialist party to form a new government on Saturday as expected.
Riot police put an end to a 10-hour siege of parliament in the early hours of Saturday, firing blank cartridges and using clubs to clear a path to evacuate deputies.
Around mid-morning, about 500 to 600 people gathered peacefully around the cathedral and the nearby parliament building, which was still surrounded by riot police and troops.
The opposition asked its supporters to meet at the cathedral to hear the head of the party's parliamentary group give an account of the meeting with Zhelev.
